display.purpose: The live score on the playfield. Fluid, snapped to the 20 px grid, 40 px minimum.

headline.purpose: Title lettering on the sky. Fluid, snapped to the 20 px grid, 40 px minimum.

title.purpose: Board headings, card headline, primary button label, the verdict percentage.

body.purpose: All other text. Labels are body type in soft ink.

shadows.name: board-bevel
shadows.purpose: Stepped bevel on boards, the crash and pause card, the title-screen note.

shadows.name: button-primary
shadows.purpose: Primary button bevel plus the 4px plum base that collapses on press.

shadows.name: button-quiet
shadows.purpose: Quiet button bevel plus the 4px plum base.

shadows.name: meter-shade
shadows.purpose: Bottom step on the green meter fill.

shadows.name: sky-type-drop
shadows.purpose: One-step hard drop under white outlined type on the playfield (a filter, paired with a 0.1em plum text stroke).

motion.name: button-press
motion.purpose: Button moves down 4px and its base collapses on :active.

motion.name: score-pop
motion.purpose: The score settles on each point.

motion.name: card-rise
motion.purpose: The paused or crashed card arrives.

motion.name: crash-flash
motion.purpose: White wash over the canvas on a crash.

motion.name: wing-beat
motion.purpose: Bird wing cycle; in flight it beats only while rising.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes the press transition, score pop, card rise, crash flash, title bob and idle wing beat.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one orange action on screen: Let Jev fly, Fly again, Try again.
components.css: .ds-btn { font-family: 'Jersey 20', ui-monospace, 'Courier New', monospace; font-weight: 400; font-size: 40px; line-height: 1; color: #fffdf2; background: #e86a17; border: 4px solid #543847; border-radius: 0; padding: 8px 20px 12px; box-shadow: inset 0 4px 0 #f7a43c, inset 0 -4px 0 #a8440a, 0 4px 0 #543847; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 80ms ease-out, box-shadow 80ms ease-out; } .ds-btn:hover { background: #f07a25; } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(4px); box-shadow: inset 0 4px 0 #f7a43c, inset 0 -4px 0 #a8440a, 0 0 0 #543847; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid #3b2832; outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-btn:disabled { background: #d3c27a; color: #6a4f45; cursor: not-allowed; box-shadow: inset 0 4px 0 #e9dba0, inset 0 -4px 0 #b8a660, 0 4px 0 #543847; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-btn { transition: none; } }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.description: The lesser action on a board or card: Stop, Stop Jev, Forget everything.
components.css: .ds-btn-quiet { font-family: 'Jersey 20', ui-monospace, 'Courier New', monospace; font-weight: 400; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1; color: #3b2832; background: #e9dba0; border: 4px solid #543847; border-radius: 0; padding: 8px 12px 10px; box-shadow: inset 0 4px 0 #f6edc4, inset 0 -4px 0 #d3c27a, 0 4px 0 #543847; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 80ms ease-out, box-shadow 80ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-quiet:hover { background: #f6edc4; } .ds-btn-quiet:active { transform: translateY(4px); box-shadow: inset 0 4px 0 #f6edc4, inset 0 -4px 0 #d3c27a, 0 0 0 #543847; } .ds-btn-quiet:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid #3b2832; outline-offset: 4px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-btn-quiet { transition: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The world is the category canon, and it is the user's choice. Asked in a structured question over a rolled direction, Swarnim picked: "Classic arcade look: blue sky, green pipes, a chunky bird, big score at the top. My own drawing in that style, not the original game's artwork." Everything here follows from that sentence. The playfield is an arcade cabinet in daylight: sky blue, green pipes, a striped ground, a yellow bird, a big white score. Nothing on it is a copy of the original sprites; every shape is drawn in code for this project.

Beside the cabinet sit two tan boards, the same tan the arcade uses for its scoreboard. They are the clipboard: one shows the pilot's live answer (what it was told, how sure it was, how long it took), the other what its crashes have taught it. The boards borrow the cabinet's materials (plum outline, stepped bevel, pixel type) so the reading surface and the game read as one object. The page around them is a single dark teal surround that carries no content.

The system is flat, square and stepped. There is one typeface at one weight, one outline colour, no gradients, no blur and no rounded corners. The direction refuses the dark AI-dashboard look: the product is about a model's decisions, and it shows them on daylight tan in plain words, never on a dark panel of charts.
keyCharacteristics: One typeface, Jersey 20, at one weight, set only on its 20 px grid.
Plum is the only outline colour: 4 px in the page, 2 px in the canvas art.
Flat fills everywhere; depth is a stepped bevel, never a blur or a gradient.
Square corners throughout; curves exist only as 2 px stair-steps in the art.
All art is drawn in code on a 2 px grid in a 360 x 640 world. No image files.
Daylight palette: sky, green and tan carry the surface; the dark surround is only the room.

rules.name: The Plum Line Rule
rules.body: Every outline in the system is `plum`. Black is not used for outlines, text or shadow anywhere.

rules.name: The Green Means Flap Rule
rules.body: In the page, green appears in exactly one place: the meter fill when the answer is at or over 50%. Below the line the fill is `ink-soft`. Green is never decoration on the boards.

rules.name: The One Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange is the primary button. There is one primary button on screen at a time, and no other element takes the orange fill.

rules.name: The Daylight Rule
rules.body: Content sits on sky, tan or cream. `surround` is the room around the cabinet; nothing is ever set on it.

rules.name: The Twenty Grid Rule
rules.body: Jersey 20 is set only at multiples of 20 px. Fixed sizes in the build are 20 and 40; the two fluid sizes snap with `round(px / 20) * 20` and never go below 40. A size between grid steps blurs the face and is a bug.

rules.name: The Outline On Sky Rule
rules.body: Type that sits directly on the playfield is `white` with a `plum` outline (0.1em stroke painted under the fill) and a one-step hard `plum` drop of 0.05em. Type on tan or cream is plain `ink` with no outline and no shadow.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Weight 400 only. Emphasis is a size step up the grid, never bold.

rules.name: The Stepped Bevel Rule
rules.body: Depth is a 4px light step and a 4px dark step, inset. Every shadow in the system has zero blur and zero horizontal offset.

rules.name: The Base Is For Pressing Rule
rules.body: Only something that can be pressed carries the outer 4px plum base. Boards, cards and wells never get an outer shadow.

rules.name: The Drawn In Code Rule
rules.body: Art is this project's own drawing, made of rectangles on the 2 px grid. No image files, no sprites from the original game, no anti-aliased vector shapes.

dos: Do set Jersey 20 only at multiples of 20 px, at weight 400, with `font-synthesis: none`.
Do outline everything in `plum`: 4px solid in the page, 2 px in the canvas art.
Do show depth with the 4px stepped bevel (lighter step inside the top edge, darker step inside the bottom edge).
Do draw new art in code, with flat fills on the 2 px grid of the 360 x 640 world, and build curves from stair-steps.
Do put content on sky, tan or cream, and keep the tan boards the same materials as the arcade scoreboard.
Do keep white outlined type for lettering that sits directly on the playfield, and plain `ink` for type on tan.
Do reserve space for values that change length, so a board does not move while it is being read.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion` by removing the movement, as the build does.
donts: Don't use the original game's artwork or trace it. The user chose their own drawing in that style.
Don't build a dark AI-dashboard: no dark panels, no content on `surround`, no glow.
Don't round a corner, blur a shadow or draw a gradient. All three are absent from the build.
Don't use orange for anything but the one primary button, or green in the page for anything but a "flap" answer.
Don't use pure black or pure white; the darks are warm plum-browns and the lightest tint is the warm `white`.
Don't add a second typeface or a bold weight.
Don't give a board, card or well an outer shadow; the plum base belongs to things that press.
Don't animate the probability meter between answers.
